claims.statement: The app uses the @vercel/sandbox SDK (declared as `"@vercel/sandbox": "^0.0.21"` in package.json) to provision ephemeral Linux VMs, imported uniformly as `import { Sandbox } from '@vercel/sandbox'` across `lib/sandbox/creation.ts`, `lib/sandbox/commands.ts`, `lib/sandbox/git.ts`, `lib/sandbox/sandbox-registry.ts`, and every agent adapter under `lib/sandbox/agents/`.

The codebase touches exactly five SDK call sites: `Sandbox.create` (provisioning), `Sandbox.get` (cross-execution reconnect), and the instance methods `sandbox.runCommand`, `sandbox.domain`, `sandbox.stop` — plus the readonly `sandbox.sandboxId` accessor.

`Sandbox.create` is called from exactly two places: `lib/sandbox/creation.ts:99` (the canonical new-task builder, which does NOT pass the SDK's `source` option and instead clones the repo manually inside the VM via `mkdir -p /vercel/sandbox/project && git clone --depth 1 <authenticated-url>`), and `app/api/tasks/[taskId]/start-sandbox/route.ts:91` (the keep-alive rehydration endpoint, which DOES pass `source: { type: 'git', url, revision, depth: 1 }` and uses a single detected port rather than the default `[3000, 5173]`).

`Sandbox.get` is the cross-execution reconnect primitive — because the in-memory `Map<taskId, Sandbox>` in `lib/sandbox/sandbox-registry.ts` is local to a single serverless execution, any later request (continue, terminal, file ops, sandbox-health, restart-dev, merge-pr, stop-sandbox, sync-changes, autocomplete, lsp, and the file routes) must re-attach by `sandboxId` using the canonical shape `Sandbox.get({ sandboxId, teamId, projectId, token })`; `Sandbox.get` failures have no shared retry helper, with each route owning its own recovery strategy.

`sandbox.runCommand` is invoked in two distinct signatures: a positional form `sandbox.runCommand(command, args)` used by the wrappers in `lib/sandbox/commands.ts` (`runCommandInSandbox`, `runInProject`, `runStreamingCommandInSandbox`) whose result has `exitCode` plus `stdout`/`stderr` as functions returning `Promise<string>` wrapped in try/catch; and an options-object form `sandbox.runCommand({ cmd, args, cwd, sudo, detached, stdout, stderr })` used in `creation.ts:448`, `agents/claude.ts:415`, `start-sandbox/route.ts:285`, and `terminal/route.ts:74` to pass streaming and lifecycle flags the positional form does not support.

`sandbox.domain(port)` returns the public HTTPS URL for a forwarded VM port and is called from exactly three places: `creation.ts:460` after a 3000 ms wait following the detached dev-server `runCommand`, `creation.ts:474` as a fallback when no dev script was detected (using the default port, switched to `5173` for Vite projects detected via `vite` in `dependencies`/`devDependencies`), and `start-sandbox/route.ts:297` after the same 3-second wait.

`sandbox.stop()` is the SDK-level shutdown primitive distinct from `shutdownSandbox` in `lib/sandbox/git.ts:75` (which is a best-effort `pkill -f node|python|npm|yarn|pnpm` and explicitly documents that no explicit shutdown method is available); it is called from exactly three places — `sandbox-registry.ts:49` inside `killSandbox` (catches rejection as success), `stop-sandbox/route.ts:44`, and `merge-pr/route.ts:66` (which ignores the `keepAlive` flag and treats merge as definitive end-of-life).

The detached dev-server log capture uses two `Writable` streams (`captureServerStdout`, `captureServerStderr`) constructed with `new Writable({ write(chunk, _encoding, callback) { ... } })` that split each chunk on `\n`, prefix non-empty lines with `[SERVER]`, and forward them via `TaskLogger.info`; the streams are passed to `sandbox.runCommand({ cmd: 'sh', args: ['-c', 'cd /vercel/sandbox/project && <devCommand>'], detached: true, stdout: captureServerStdout, stderr: captureServerStderr })`, with the `write` callback always invoking `callback()` to avoid deadlocking the SDK's stream pump and `logger.info(...).catch(() => {})` swallowing any rejected logger promise.

The SDK requires three environment variables on every call — `SANDBOX_VERCEL_TEAM_ID`, `SANDBOX_VERCEL_PROJECT_ID`, and `SANDBOX_VERCEL_TOKEN` — listed in the Vercel deploy URL at `lib/constants.ts:9`, validated up front by `validateEnvironmentVariables` in `lib/sandbox/config.ts` (which surfaces `'SANDBOX_VERCEL_TEAM_ID is required for sandbox creation'` etc. on failure), and passed as `process.env.SANDBOX_VERCEL_*!` to every `Sandbox.create` and `Sandbox.get` call; `lib/utils/logging.ts:25-30` has dedicated regexes that redact the token from any logged command string.

The SDK surfaces exactly two values that the database persists across serverless executions, both written to text columns on the `tasks` row (`sandbox_id`, `sandbox_url`): `sandbox.sandboxId` is the opaque SDK identifier and the argument to every `Sandbox.get` call (the durable "control plane" handle for "which VM does this task own"); `sandbox.domain(port)` is the public HTTPS URL loaded by the browser preview iframe and pinged by `sandbox-health` with `AbortSignal.timeout(5000)` (the "data plane" handle for the dev server).

The canonical project directory inside the sandbox is exported as `PROJECT_DIR = '/vercel/sandbox/project'` from `lib/sandbox/commands.ts:4`; every `runInProject` wrapper executes `cd /vercel/sandbox/project && <command>` via `sh -c`, every terminal-command `runCommand` from the API passes `cwd: PROJECT_DIR`, and `git status`/`git add`/`git commit`/`git push` operations all run in this directory.

`Sandbox.create` errors are caught at `creation.ts:140-163` and translated into either a `'Sandbox creation timed out after 5 minutes'` user-facing message when `error.code === 'ETIMEDOUT'`, `error.name === 'TimeoutError'`, or the message contains `'timeout'`, or a rethrow after `logger.error('Sandbox creation failed')` for any other failure — this is the canonical error-translation point for VM provisioning failures.

The dev server is launched with `detached: true` so the `runCommand` promise resolves immediately while the dev server keeps running inside the VM for the duration of the agent's work — this is what allows the browser preview iframe to remain live across the agent's file edits and is the reason the SDK's `sandbox.domain(port)` must be called after a 3-second `setTimeout` wait for the server to bind.

`createSandbox` does not use the SDK's `source.git.url` parameter but instead manually clones the repo inside the VM so that `createAuthenticatedRepoUrl` in `lib/sandbox/config.ts:69` can embed the user's GitHub PAT as the username and `x-oauth-basic` as the password for `github.com` URLs — the SDK's `source` path does not expose a hook to inject authenticated clone URLs, which is the architectural reason the canonical new-task builder passes no `source` to `Sandbox.create`.
